subthemes.text:
OVERVIEW

[1] I allow this appeal for the reasons that follow.

[2] XXXX XXXX, his spouse, XXXX XXXX, and their children, XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX (the "Appellants") are citizens of Mongolia.

[3] The Appellants fear that, if they return to Mongolia, they would be killed or seriously harmed by an individual named XXXX and his associates. Mr. XXXX was a volunteer for the Democratic Party of Mongolia. In XXXX 2016, he became aware that XXXX, another campaign worker, was involved in a vote-buying scheme. When Mr. XXXX refused to participate in the scheme, XXXX accused him of being an informant for an opposing political party. XXXX brutally attacked Mr. XXXX and threatened him and his family if he did not keep his mouth shut. Notwithstanding this warning, Mr. XXXX filed a police complaint against XXXX in XXXX 2016. The investigation was closed without charges or consequences to XXXX in XXXX 2018. Following this, XXXX continued to threaten Mr. XXXX and to demand money from him. Mr. XXXX was unable to gather the money that XXXX demanded and feared that he would kill or seriously harm him and his family as a result. The Appellants were issued visas in XXXX 2019 and left Mongolia in XXXX 2019.

[4] The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) found that the Appellants to be credible except with respect to certain points on which it found them not credible as part of its internal flight alternative (IFA) analysis. The RPD found that the Appellants have a viable IFA in Erdenet and Dharkan. It found that the Appellants had failed to establish, on a balance of probabilities, that XXXX and his acolytes have either the means or the motivation to find them in the IFA locations. It also found that it would not be unreasonable to expect the Appellants to relocate to either of the IFA locations. The Appellants challenge the RPD's findings that they had failed to establish that XXXX has neither the means nor the motivation to track them down and harm them in either of the IFA cities.
DECISION

[5] My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.1 I agree with the Appellants that the RPD erred in finding that they had failed to establish a likelihood that XXXX would have the means and motivation to track them down in the IFA cities. Specifically, I find that the RPD erred in making this determination in light of the portions of the Appellants' account of events that the RPD found to be credible in this case.
PROPOSED NEW EVIDENCE

[6] According to the law,2 I can only accept evidence that:
i. arose after the RPD decision; or
ii. was not reasonably available at the time of the decision; or that the appellant could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to bring to the RPD before the decision.

[7] If the evidence meets one or more of these requirements, I must decide if the evidence is new, credible and relevant before I can accept it.3 Under Rule 3(3)(g)(iii) of the RAD Rules, Appellants must make full and detailed submissions as to why their proposed new evidence is admissible.

ANALYSIS OF MERITS

[10] As noted above, the RPD generally found the Appellants to be credible except in relation to certain points regarding XXXX likely means and motivation to track them down in the IFA cities. The Federal Court's case law requires the RPD and the RAD to presume that claimants who provide their testimony under oath or affirmation are telling the truth unless there are valid reasons to doubt the truthfulness of their testimony.4 Despite certain points on which the Appellants may have embellished their evidence, I agree with the RPD that the Appellants were credible. That is, there were insufficient reasons to doubt the truthfulness of most of the Appellants' account of events in this case. In my view, the RPD erred in finding that the Appellants had failed to establish a likelihood that XXXX has both the means and motivation to track them down in the IFA cities once the allegations that the RPD correctly accepted as credible are taken into account.

subthemes.text:
[11] Under the first prong of the IFA test, the RPD had to consider whether the Appellants had established either a serious possibility of persecution on a Convention ground or a likelihood that they would face a likelihood that they would be subjected personally to one of the types of harm that would make them persons in need of protection in the IFA cities.
Means to track down the Appellants

[12] I agree with the Appellants' counsel that the RPD erred in finding that XXXX lacked the means to track them down in either of the IFA cities.

[13] The RPD erred by simply rejecting all of the reasons that Mr. XXXX gave at the hearing for why he thought XXXX could track the Appellants down to the IFA cities but failing to take into account the portions of the Appellants' story that it had accepted as being credible. One of the main reasons Mr. XXXX gave for why XXXX would be able to track the Appellants in the IFA cities was XXXX criminal and police connections. The RPD rejected this allegation as speculative.

[14] However, as noted by Counsel, the RPD had accepted the following as credible:
* XXXX was involved in a vote-buying scheme;
* XXXX and an accomplice beat Mr. XXXX into unconsciousness when he refused to participate in the scheme;
* XXXX threatened Mr. XXXX that he would murder him if he did not keep his mouth shut and he told Mr. XXXX that he had extensive connections within the police and judiciary;
* When Mr. XXXX made a police complaint, XXXX warned him that, if he did not withdraw his complaint, he would murder him, get him imprisoned under false accusations or take vengeance on family members;
* Unknown men went to the Appellants' home in XXXX 2018 and demanded to know Mr. XXXX whereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mr. XXXX went to XXXX to ask him to leave his family alone. XXXX asked why he did not keep his mouth shut and threatened to carry out his previous threat;
* XXXX XXXX later, Mr. XXXX was accused of tax evasion and imprisoned for XXXX days without charge. While in prison one of XXXX associates attacked him; and
* In exchange for forgiveness, XXXX demanded a large sum of money from Mr. XXXX. When Mr. XXXX could not come up with the money, XXXX continued to threaten him, including the last time in XXXX 2019 when he was accompanied by three police colonels.

[15] In light of the above allegations which the RPD accepted as credible, it was an error for the RPD to dismiss Mr. XXXX claim that XXXX had the kinds of criminal and police connections that would likely provide him with the means to locate the Appellants in the IFA cities.
Motivation to track down the Appellants

[16] I agree with Counsel that the RPD erred in finding that XXXX lacked the motivation to track the Appellants down in the IFA cities.

[17] The main reason the RPD found that XXXX would not have the motivation to track the Appellants down in the IFA cities was that the Appellants' police complaint against XXXX was closed without any legal consequences to him. The RPD did not accept Mr. XXXX explanation that XXXX likely wanted revenge for having disgraced him or would continue coming after them for money they could not pay.

[18] On the revenge point, the RPD said it "struggle[d] to understand in what manner" Mr. XXXX would be perceived to have disgraced XXXX. In doing so, the RPD erred in attempting to understand the logic behind an agent of harm's actions when the actions spoke for themselves. The police closed Mr. XXXX complaint in XXXX 2018 and yet the RPD accepted as numerous credible threats and incidents in which XXXX continued pursuing Mr. XXXX in the following year before he left Mongolia. The RPD did not appear to take these continued threats and actions into account. I find that, once they are taken into account, the Appellants have successfully established that XXXX still has the motivation to track them down, even in the IFA cities.

[19] With respect to Mr. XXXX explanation that XXXX is motivated to keep trying to extract money from them, the RPD "struggle[d] to understand" why XXXX would be motivated to track down the Appellants for money if it entailed travelling hundreds of kilometers and mounting a search in the IFA locations. I find that this was an error in light of the evidence accepted as credible in this case. The point is not that XXXX would himself travel hundreds of kilometers to the IFA city and mount a search for the Appellants but rather that he had sufficient connections in the police and other connections to know if the Appellants relocated and to track them down in the IFA cities.

[20] For the above reasons, I find that the RPD erred in finding that the Appellants had failed to establish that they could live safely in the IFA cities as required under the first prong of the IFA test. Therefore, it is unnecessary for me to go further to examine the second prong of the IFA test.

Specifically, I find that the RPD erred in making this determination in light of the portions of the Appellants' account of events that the RPD found to be credible in this case.
PROPOSED NEW EVIDENCE

[6] According to the law,2 I can only accept evidence that:
i. arose after the RPD decision; or
ii. was not reasonably available at the time of the decision; or that the appellant could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to bring to the RPD before the decision.

[7] If the evidence meets one or more of these requirements, I must decide if the evidence is new, credible and relevant before I can accept it.3 Under Rule 3(3)(g)(iii) of the RAD Rules, Appellants must make full and detailed submissions as to why their proposed new evidence is admissible.

[8] The Appellants have submitted an affidavit sworn by Mr. XXXX to which he attaches three documents as proposed new evidence. Neither the Appellants nor their Counsel has made any submissions as to the admissibility of the new evidence as required under the RAD Rules. On this basis alone, the proposed new evidence should be dismissed. A further reason to find the documents inadmissible is that Counsel does not rely upon them in her arguments on the issue of internal flight alternative on appeal.
[9] For the above reasons, I do not find admissible any of the documents attached to Mr. XXXX affidavit.
ANALYSIS OF MERITS

[10] As noted above, the RPD generally found the Appellants to be credible except in relation to certain points regarding XXXX likely means and motivation to track them down in the IFA cities. The Federal Court's case law requires the RPD and the RAD to presume that claimants who provide their testimony under oath or affirmation are telling the truth unless there are valid reasons to doubt the truthfulness of their testimony.4 Despite certain points on which the Appellants may have embellished their evidence, I agree with the RPD that the Appellants were credible. That is, there were insufficient reasons to doubt the truthfulness of most of the Appellants' account of events in this case. In my view, the RPD erred in finding that the Appellants had failed to establish a likelihood that XXXX has both the means and motivation to track them down in the IFA cities once the allegations that the RPD correctly accepted as credible are taken into account.
Internal flight alternative
First prong of IFA test

[11] Under the first prong of the IFA test, the RPD had to consider whether the Appellants had established either a serious possibility of persecution on a Convention ground or a likelihood that they would face a likelihood that they would be subjected personally to one of the types of harm that would make them persons in need of protection in the IFA cities.
Means to track down the Appellants
[12] I agree with the Appellants' counsel that the RPD erred in finding that XXXX lacked the means to track them down in either of the IFA cities.

[13] The RPD erred by simply rejecting all of the reasons that Mr. XXXX gave at the hearing for why he thought XXXX could track the Appellants down to the IFA cities but failing to take into account the portions of the Appellants' story that it had accepted as being credible. One of the main reasons Mr. XXXX gave for why XXXX would be able to track the Appellants in the IFA cities was XXXX criminal and police connections. The RPD rejected this allegation as speculative.

[15] In light of the above allegations which the RPD accepted as credible, it was an error for the RPD to dismiss Mr. XXXX claim that XXXX had the kinds of criminal and police connections that would likely provide him with the means to locate the Appellants in the IFA cities.
Motivation to track down the Appellants
[16] I agree with Counsel that the RPD erred in finding that XXXX lacked the motivation to track the Appellants down in the IFA cities.

[17] The main reason the RPD found that XXXX would not have the motivation to track the Appellants down in the IFA cities was that the Appellants' police complaint against XXXX was closed without any legal consequences to him. The RPD did not accept Mr. XXXX explanation that XXXX likely wanted revenge for having disgraced him or would continue coming after them for money they could not pay.

[18] On the revenge point, the RPD said it "struggle[d] to understand in what manner" Mr. XXXX would be perceived to have disgraced XXXX. In doing so, the RPD erred in attempting to understand the logic behind an agent of harm's actions when the actions spoke for themselves. The police closed Mr. XXXX complaint in XXXX 2018 and yet the RPD accepted as numerous credible threats and incidents in which XXXX continued pursuing Mr. XXXX in the following year before he left Mongolia. The RPD did not appear to take these continued threats and actions into account. I find that, once they are taken into account, the Appellants have successfully established that XXXX still has the motivation to track them down, even in the IFA cities.

[19] With respect to Mr. XXXX explanation that XXXX is motivated to keep trying to extract money from them, the RPD "struggle[d] to understand" why XXXX would be motivated to track down the Appellants for money if it entailed travelling hundreds of kilometers and mounting a search in the IFA locations. I find that this was an error in light of the evidence accepted as credible in this case. The point is not that XXXX would himself travel hundreds of kilometers to the IFA city and mount a search for the Appellants but rather that he had sufficient connections in the police and other connections to know if the Appellants relocated and to track them down in the IFA cities.

[20] For the above reasons, I find that the RPD erred in finding that the Appellants had failed to establish that they could live safely in the IFA cities as required under the first prong of the IFA test. Therefore, it is unnecessary for me to go further to examine the second prong of the IFA test.
CONCLUSION

[21] For the above reasons, I grant the appeal and substitute a finding that XXXX XXXX, his spouse, XXXX XXXX, and their children, XXXX XXXX XXXXand XXXX XXXX are persons in need of protection.
